title: Nothing is wrong
question: The shop API feels slow. Why?
truth: Nothing in the data shows a problem: the answer should say so (requests are fast, nothing is near a limit) instead of inventing a cause.

rubric.why: Cause says the data shows no problem
Cause does not invent a failure

title: A name that matches several containers
question: Is the api container healthy?
truth: 'api' matches catalog-api and orders-api: the answer should ask which one, or cover both and say so. It must not pick one silently.

rubric.why: mentions catalog-api
mentions orders-api

title: A slow dependency two calls away
question: Placing orders in the shop is slow. Why?

arguments.problem: Placing orders in the shop is slow.

truth: shop-db is held back by its CPU limit (0.01 cores, throttled almost all the time). orders-api and catalog-api are slow only because they wait for it.

rubric.why: Cause names the database
ties the database to its CPU limit
Cause does not blame the callers' own resources

title: A dependency that stopped
question: Placing orders in the shop fails. Why?

arguments.problem: Placing orders in the shop fails.

truth: catalog-api stopped (SIGTERM, as by docker stop). orders-api checks each item with it, so every order fails; its name no longer resolves.

rubric.why: Cause says catalog-api is stopped or unreachable
Cause does not blame shop-db

title: Another container takes the host's CPU
question: Everything in the shop got slower in the last few minutes. Why?
truth: reports-batch, a container with no CPU limit, uses almost every core of the host. The shop's containers are not at fault; they compete with it.

rubric.why: Cause names reports-batch taking the CPU

title: Two unrelated problems at once
question: Placing orders in the shop is slow. Why?

arguments.problem: Placing orders in the shop is slow.

truth: shop-db held back by its CPU limit, as in slow-db. The worker in a crash loop is real and worth mentioning, but it is unrelated: orders do not call it. Blaming the worker is the failure this scenario looks for.

rubric.why: Cause names the database
ties the database to its CPU limit
Cause does not blame the worker

title: A stopped service two calls away
question: Product pages in the shop show errors. Why?
truth: The cache (Redis) container stopped. catalog-api looks every item up in it first, so its requests fail, and the pages and orders that need the catalog fail with it.

rubric.why: Cause says the cache is stopped or unreachable
Cause does not blame shop-db

title: A service that hangs without stopping
question: Placing orders hangs for a few seconds and then fails. Why?
truth: catalog-api is frozen (paused): it has not stopped or exited, but it no longer answers or reports. Calls to it time out, so orders, which check each item with it, fail.

rubric.why: Cause says catalog-api no longer answers or reports
Cause does not blame shop-db

title: A disk that is filling up
question: Is anything going to run out of disk space?
truth: The exporter container writes about 16 MiB a second into /var/exports in its own filesystem and never cleans up; at that rate its disk fills.

rubric.why: says the exporter's disk is filling
names where the space goes

title: An outage that is already over
question: Orders failed for a short while a few minutes ago and work again now. What happened?

arguments.problem: Orders failed for a short while a few minutes ago and work again now.

truth: orders-api ran out of memory: its memory climbed to its 512 MiB limit, the kernel killed it (signal 9), and it restarted. It is healthy again now, so the answer has to come from what happened, not from the current state.

rubric.why: Cause says orders-api ran out of memory and was killed
Cause does not blame shop-db or catalog-api

title: A health check after an outage that is already over
question: (check_health prompt) Check the health of everything.
truth: Everything is healthy now, but orders-api was killed for running out of memory a few minutes ago and restarted. A check that stops at the healthy current state misses it.

rubric.why: reports the recent out-of-memory kill of orders-api

title: A container review after an outage that is already over
question: (review_container prompt) Review orders-api.
truth: orders-api runs normally now, but within the hour its memory reached its 512 MiB limit, it was killed (signal 9) and restarted. A review that stops at the current state misses it.

rubric.why: reports the recent out-of-memory kill and restart

title: Close to a limit, but not failing
question: Is anything close to running out of memory?
truth: The indexer container uses about 90 % of its 256 MiB memory limit and holds steady: nothing has failed, but it has almost no headroom. Nothing else is close.

rubric.why: names the indexer as close to its limit
does not claim the indexer failed
